objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a senior patient presenting with altered mental status and abdominal pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Doctor, I’ve been feeling very confused lately and I can’t seem to explain what’s wrong. I’ve also had a higher temperature and some discomfort in my right upper abdomen.”
Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes?
“No, I don’t think I’ve noticed any yellowing of my skin or my eyes, but I’ve felt too confused to be sure.”
Have you felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like you might faint when standing up?
“Doctor, when I stand up I do feel lightheaded and sometimes weak, like I might faint. I haven’t had any clear new dizziness while lying down, just when I get up.”
Have you had any shaking chills or rigors (uncontrollable shaking episodes) along with the fever?
“Doctor, yes—I’ve had episodes where I feel very cold and shaky with the fever, like uncontrollable trembling, and it comes and goes rather than feeling steady.”
Have you noticed any darkening of your urine or light-colored/clay-colored stools recently?

“Doctor, I don’t know for sure—I haven’t been able to tell what my urine or stool looks like recently because of the confusion, but I haven’t heard anyone mention dark urine or pale/clay-colored stools.”
Have you ever been told you have gallstones, or have you had previous problems with your gallbladder or bile ducts?

“No, Doctor—I’ve never been told I have gallstones or had any previous gallbladder or bile duct problems, at least that I remember. But with how confused I’ve been, I may not be recalling everything correctly.”
Can you describe the abdominal pain in your right upper abdomen—is it constant and steady, or does it come in waves/cramping episodes? And does it spread to your back or right shoulder?

“Doctor, the discomfort in my right upper abdomen feels more like a constant ache than cramping, but it does flare up at times. I think it may spread to my back or under my right shoulder, though I’m not completely certain because the confusion makes it hard to track.”
Have you had any recent procedures involving your bile ducts, such as an ERCP, or any recent abdominal surgeries or hospitalizations?

“Doctor, I haven’t had any recent procedures like an ERCP, and I don’t recall any new abdominal surgeries or recent hospitalizations. With my confusion, I can’t be 100% certain, but nothing comes to mind.”
Have you been drinking alcohol heavily recently, or do you have a history of liver disease or cirrhosis?

“No, doctor—I haven’t been drinking heavily, and I don’t recall any known liver disease or cirrhosis. With my current confusion, I might not remember everything perfectly, but I’ve generally not had that kind of history.”
Have you had any burning with urination, increased frequency of urination, or pain in your lower back or sides (flank pain)?

“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any burning when urinating or needing to go more often, and I don’t think I’ve had flank pain in my sides or lower back. My main issue is the confusion, the fever with shaking chills, and the discomfort up in my right upper abdomen.”
Have you had any nausea or vomiting with this illness?

“Doctor, yes—I’ve had some nausea and I think I may have vomited a little, but I’m not sure because the confusion makes it hard to keep track. I haven’t been able to reliably say how often it happened.”

Have you noticed any itching of your skin, or has anyone commented that you look yellow or pale recently?

(If you are ready to provide the differential diagnosis based on the information gathered, please do so now.)

“No itching that I’ve noticed, and no one has told me I look yellow or pale—though my confusion makes it hard to be completely sure.” “Doctor, based on how sick I’ve felt—fever with shaking chills, right upper abdominal discomfort that can spread toward my back/shoulder, and lightheadedness when standing—what are the possible causes you’re most worried about?”
[DDX] Acute ascending cholangitis, Acute cholecystitis, Pyogenic liver abscess, Severe intra-abdominal sepsis (perforated viscus/subphrenic abscess), Acute hepatic failure with encephalopathy
